stemBlocks.value: Using a ruler, a pencil and a pair of compasses, construct triangle XYZ such that XY = 7 cm, YZ = 6 cm and XZ = 8 cm. (i) Measure and state the size of angle XYZ.
Think first: Three given sides means a pure arc construction — no angles are drawn at all.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p162-q21 from workbook page 162.

solutionSteps.instruction: With centre X and radius 8 cm, draw an arc above XY.

contentBlocks.value: This arc is every point at the correct distance XZ

solutionSteps.instruction: With centre Y and radius 6 cm, draw a second arc cutting the first.

contentBlocks.value: The crossing point is the only point at both correct distances

solutionSteps.instruction: Join XZ and YZ, then measure ∠XYZ with a protractor.

strategyBlocks.value: Draw XY = 7 cm, swing an arc of radius 8 cm from X and one of radius 6 cm from Y; their intersection is Z. Then measure ∠XYZ.

whyThisWorks.value: Three sides fix a triangle completely — that is the SSS congruence condition — so the two arcs can only cross in one place on a given side of XY. The cosine rule is the algebraic form of the same fact: from three sides it returns one and only one value for each angle, which is why it can verify a measured construction.

commonErrors.misconception: Drawing the arcs with the radii swapped (8 cm from Y, 6 cm from X), producing a mirror triangle.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Drawing the arcs with the radii swapped (8 cm from Y, 6 cm from X), producing a mirror triangle.

commonErrors.misconception: Erasing the arcs, losing the construction marks.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Erasing the arcs, losing the construction marks.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the outer scale of the protractor and writing 104.5° instead of 75.5°.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the outer scale of the protractor and writing 104.5° instead of 75.5°.

examTip.value: After measuring an angle, check it against the side lengths: the largest angle must face the longest side. Here XZ = 8 cm is longest, so ∠XYZ must be the biggest angle — and it is.
